subject: mass-communication
title: Television in India
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Television ______ and creates ______ about social issues like climate change.
Fill in the blanks: ______ and ______ are emerging trends in television transmission.
State true or false: (i) Lighting establishes the mood in television production. (ii) Television viewing is the only purpose of entertainment.
Name the first television service and the year.
Fill in the blanks: Doordarshan became a separate department in ______; Prasar Bharati was established in ______.
State true or false: (i) Increased exposure to violence on TV can lead to violent behaviour in some children. (ii) Television is bad for children.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: List any two emerging trends in television transmission.
questions.answer: Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) and mobile TV broadcasting (also DTH and cable).

questions.q: Discuss any two positive impacts of television in our daily lives.
questions.answer: It educates and informs (SITE, educational channels) and creates awareness about issues such as pollution, and it entertains.

questions.q: What is IPTV?
questions.answer: Internet Protocol Television that lets viewers watch, record and share television on computers and mobile phones through the internet and a set-top box.

questions.q: What is the importance of 1982 in Indian television history?
questions.answer: Doordarshan gave national coverage for the first time through INSAT 1A and the first colour transmission during the Ninth Asian Games.

questions.q: What is a pay channel?
questions.answer: A channel that charges the cable operator a certain amount per subscriber per month, e.g. Sony and Star Plus.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Discuss any two positive and two negative impacts of television.
questions.answer: Positive: education and awareness. Negative: violence and aggression in children; stereotypes and consumerism (also couch potato and obesity).

questions.q: List three milestones in the history of television in India.
questions.answer: 1959 experimental start; 1975–76 SITE; 1982 national colour coverage by INSAT 1A (also 1976 Doordarshan separated, 1997 Prasar Bharati).

questions.q: Explain how private channels emerged in India.
questions.answer: The Gulf War coverage by CNN led to satellite dishes and cable; STAR and an Indian company created Zee TV; the Supreme Court ruling of 1995 broke the government's monopoly of airwaves; regional channels followed.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: How does television influence our daily lives? Discuss its positive and negative effects.
questions.answer: It educates, creates awareness, widens horizons and entertains; but ads tempt, couch potato habits and obesity, stereotypes and violence affect people, especially children; its effect depends on use.

questions.q: Outline the new trends in television.
questions.answer: Terrestrial, cable and direct broadcast satellite delivery; free-to-air and pay channels; mobile TV and IPTV; audience-backed and reality shows to meet the interactive challenge of new media.
